title: Influence bound for polynomial thresholds
statement:
There exists a real constant $C>0$ such that for all natural numbers $n,k$ with $2\le k$, every $\{-1,1\}$-valued function $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ represented as the threshold sign of a multilinear polynomial of degree at most $k$ satisfies
\[\operatorname{Inf}(f)\le\sqrt n\,\operatorname{rpow}\!\left(2^k\log(\max\{n,2\}),\ Ck\log(\max\{k,2\})\right).\]
Here $\operatorname{Inf}(f)$ is the sum, over coordinates, of the uniform expectation of $(f(x)-f(x^i))^2/4$, where $x^i$ is obtained by flipping coordinate $i$; the threshold sign is $1$ on nonnegative inputs and $-1$ otherwise, and $\operatorname{rpow}$ denotes real exponentiation.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ belongs to the degree-at-most-$k$ polynomial threshold class, hence is $\{-1,1\}$-valued and has such a representation
replaced:
There exists a universal real constant $C>0$ such that, for every $n,k\in\mathbb N$ with $k\geq2$ and every $f:\{0,1\}^{n}\to\{-1,1\}$ admitting a representation $f(x)=\operatorname{sgn}_{+}(p((-1)^{x_1},\ldots,(-1)^{x_n}))$ by a real multilinear polynomial $p$ of degree at most $k$,
\[
\operatorname{Inf}(f)\leq\sqrt n\,
\bigl(2^k\log(\max\{n,2\})\bigr)^{Ck\log(\max\{k,2\})}.
\]
Here $\operatorname{Inf}(f)=\sum_{i=1}^{n}\Pr_X[f(X)\neq f(X^{\{i\}})]$, $X$ is uniform, $X^{\{i\}}$ flips coordinate $i$, $\log$ is the natural logarithm, real powers have positive bases, and $\operatorname{sgn}_{+}(t)=1$ for $t\geq0$ and $-1$ for $t<0$.
